result.title: Refactor historical price feature
result.body: prior_mean(prices, index, window): at the start of index, use only the preceding window prices; index >= window > 0 and index < len(prices).
result.author: fixture-author

result.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,2 +1,4 @@
 def prior_mean(prices, index, window):
-    return sum(prices[index-window:index]) / window
+    start = index - window
+    history = prices[start:index]
+    return sum(history) / len(history)

input.body: The refactor of the `prior_mean` function introduces a potential `ZeroDivisionError` when the `window` parameter is greater than the number of preceding prices available. Specifically, if `index` is less than `window`, the function will attempt to calculate the mean of an empty list, leading to a division by zero. This needs to be addressed to ensure the function behaves correctly under all valid input conditions.
